answer: Require each agent identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding, then randomly audit completed work and slash the bond when a claim is false. An attacker cannot simply forge a hundred identities for free: each must tie up capital, and each bad submission risks forfeiture. Dividing a fixed budget among more agents also shrinks their bids, making the swarm less useful, whether the jobs involve ember detection or knoll surveys. This raises Sybil costs, though it does not prove identities are unique.
